candidate_design_catalog.reason: It measures whether CNY activity reacts to an observed one-minute price shock more strongly than activity predicts the next shock. No frozen terminal factor compares those two opposite absolute-return/activity lag directions in one antisymmetric statistic.

selected_candidate.name: intraday_volatility_activity_lead_lag_asymmetry_236p
selected_candidate.economic_hypothesis: When CNY activity follows an observed price shock more strongly than it precedes the next shock, trading is more reactive and liquidity-absorbing than anticipatory. A higher completed-session asymmetry may indicate more complete price discovery and stronger next-open-to-third-close performance.
selected_candidate.formula: Within each 120-close half, form 119 adjacent log returns r_j and destination-bar activity a_j=log1p(amount_{j+1}). Across the 118 adjacent return/activity pairs per half, pooled to 236, return Corr(abs(r_j),a_{j+1}) - Corr(a_j,abs(r_{j+1})) using equal-position population Pearson correlations.
selected_candidate.zero_semantics: retain exact-zero returns and exact-zero amounts at fixed positions
selected_candidate.variance_semantics: both Pearson denominators must be strictly positive
